papers.title: Hit Selection Using SSMD-Based Machine Learning Performance Metrics in High-Throughput Screening Assays.
papers.abstract: High-throughput screening (HTS) assays are central to early-stage drug discovery but are often limited by extreme data sparsity, as primary screens typically use only a single replicate per test substance. This sparsity makes conventional machine-learning performance metrics, such as sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), difficult to estimate empirically because they require adequately sized labeled samples. Here, we introduce a model-based framework that derives these classification metrics from the strictly standardized mean difference
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This paper introduces a model-based framework for estimating classification performance metrics (sensitivity, specificity, AUROC) in high-throughput screening when only a single replicate per compound is available. By leveraging the strictly standardized mean difference (SSMD), the approach enables hit selection and model evaluation despite extreme data sparsity. The method addresses a common limitation in early-stage drug discovery screens.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses reveal VIPR1 as a potential mediator linking environmental bisphenol A exposure to MASH-HCC progression.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC) is an increasingly important subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma, and environmental contaminants have been proposed as potential contributors to its progression. Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, has been implicated in metabolic dysfunction and liver injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking BPA exposure to MASH-HCC remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed an integrated framework combining transcriptomic analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis,
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with network analysis and experimental validation to identify VIPR1 as a potential mediator linking bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC). The findings suggest an environmental chemical exposure mechanism contributing to this increasingly common liver cancer subtype.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study used single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls, combined with machine learning, to identify maternal immune signatures associated with the condition. The analysis revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module in immune cells, offering new insights into the immune dysregulation underlying RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies.

papers.title: BAN-SDBPred: Improving Single-Stranded and Double-Stranded DNA-Binding Protein Prediction Using an Attention Network with Bilinear Convolution and Adaptive Sampling Strategy.
papers.abstract: DNA binding proteins play essential roles in numerous biological mechanisms. The DBPs can be either single-stranded binding (SSBs) or double-stranded binding (DSBs) to a DNA molecule. The in-depth identification of SSBs and DSBs has been a hot topic in bioinformatics and is involved in the drug discovery process. Traditional experimental methods failed to characterize the types of DBPs because of high cost and time constraints. While computational prediction of novel SSBs and DSBs has made significant progress, there are still challenges remaining in enhancing overall prediction performance. M
papers.summary: BAN-SDBPred is a computational tool that predicts whether a DNA-binding protein binds single-stranded or double-stranded DNA. It combines a bilinear attention network with adaptive sampling to improve prediction accuracy over existing methods. This could aid drug discovery and functional annotation of DNA-binding proteins without costly experiments.

papers.title: A Graph-Based Machine Learning Framework to Assign Empirical Interaction Parameters for Novel Molecules.
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of novel molecules are essential to modern drug discovery and related fields that require large-scale sampling of chemical space. However, obtaining accurate and robust force field parameters for novel molecules remains a major challenge. One approach to this problem is to perform quantum chemical calculations on a per-molecule basis, but doing so on a large scale is prohibitively expensive. Here, we present a graph-based machine learning framework for empirical force field assignment that scales significantly more efficiently with molecule size than quantum
papers.summary: The authors present a graph-based machine learning framework that assigns empirical force field parameters to novel molecules, avoiding the need for expensive per-molecule quantum chemical calculations. This enables more efficient large-scale molecular dynamics simulations for drug discovery and chemical space exploration.

papers.title: From Phenotypic Screening to Target and Compound Prioritization for Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is a progressive kidney disorder with limited therapeutic options, highlighting an urgent need for safer, long-term treatments. This study presents a multi-step computational and experimental approach to identify and assess target-based hypotheses for mechanisms underlying the cAMP-dependent cyst swelling. We analyzed phenotypic screening data from a 3D mIMCD3-Pkd1-/- forskolin-induced, cAMP-driven cyst swelling (CS) assay, classifying compounds based on their CS activity. These compounds were cross-referenced with the Papyrus database to id
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study combines phenotypic screening data from a 3D ADPKD cyst-swelling assay with computational target prediction using the Papyrus database to prioritize compounds and their mechanisms. The workflow links cAMP-driven cyst swelling phenotypes to potential molecular targets, offering a strategy to move from phenotypic hits toward target-based hypotheses for ADPKD drug discovery.

papers.title: Toward Imbalanced Molecular Property Regression: A Benchmark Study and Interval-Aware Mixture of Experts.
papers.abstract: Molecular property prediction is a key task in AI-driven drug discovery, yet the prevalence and impact of label imbalances in molecular property regression remain poorly understood. Through a systematic benchmark of widely used molecular property data sets, we show that target values are often highly imbalanced and that prediction errors are consistently concentrated in sparsely represented regions of the label space. We further evaluate representative imbalance-learning approaches developed for general regression tasks and find that their effectiveness on molecular data sets is limited. To ad
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks molecular property regression datasets and finds that target values are often highly imbalanced, with prediction errors concentrated in sparsely populated regions of the label space. Existing imbalance-learning methods from general regression perform poorly on these molecular datasets, so the authors propose an interval-aware mixture-of-experts approach to address the problem.

papers.title: Is AI Capable of Real-World Drug Discovery?
papers.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery frequently operates in regimes where slight structural changes have large consequences. These are situations in which current artificial intelligence (AI) methods, trained on mass data, may perform poorly. For a substantial fraction of drug-discovery projects, limited biological understanding and sparse data further constrain progress and define regimes where AI approaches remain difficult to apply. Despite these limitations, the global investment in AI continues to grow rapidly. Using two case studies characterized by structural and biochemical data, this article
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current AI methods struggle in real-world drug discovery settings where small structural changes have large biological effects and data are sparse. Using two case studies with structural and biochemical data, it highlights regimes where AI remains difficult to apply despite growing investment.

papers.title: Chemically Interpretable Explanations for Molecular Property Prediction via Fragment-Level Shapley Values.
papers.abstract: Machine learning has emerged as a powerful approach for molecular property prediction and drug discovery. However, the black-box nature of many machine learning models limits their interpretability, trustworthiness, and adoption in interdisciplinary research settings. This is especially the case in molecular machine learning, where explanations of model predictions are used for informed decision-making and downstream tasks. Shapley values, originating from cooperative game theory, provide a principled framework for attributing model predictions to individual input features. However, existing S
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper introduces a method for explaining molecular property predictions by computing Shapley values at the fragment level rather than the atom level, making the explanations more chemically interpretable. By attributing model predictions to meaningful chemical substructures, the approach bridges the gap between black-box machine learning and the chemical reasoning needed for drug discovery decisions.

papers.title: Integrative AOP-Based Mechanistic Profiling of Organic UV Filters Reveals Shared Endocrine-Metabolic and Stress-Response Pathways.
papers.abstract: Organic UV filters are widely used in personal care products and are increasingly detected in humans and the environment. Although several compounds exhibit systemic absorption and biological activity, their mechanisms of action remain poorly understood because comprehensive toxicogenomic data remain limited. Here, we developed an integrative Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP)-based framework to support the mechanistic profiling of organic UV filters with sparse experimental evidence. Molecular evidence was integrated from experimentally supported bioassay target genes, transcription factor downstr
papers.summary: This study develops an integrative Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP)-based framework to profile the mechanisms of organic UV filters, which are common in personal care products but have limited toxicogenomic data. By combining bioassay target genes and transcription factor data, the authors identify shared endocrine-metabolic and stress-response pathways across these compounds. The work provides a mechanistic basis for understanding potential health effects of UV filters despite sparse experimental evidence.

papers.title: Targeting BCL-2 through Deep Learning-Based Drug Repurposing: A Multimodal Approach Combining Diffusion-Based Generative Modeling, Neural Relational Inference, and In Vitro Validation.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of repurposable BCL-2 ligands requires not only plausible bound complex structures but also a dynamic description of how ligand binding reshapes residue-level communication. Here, we present a multimodal BCL-2 repurposing workflow built with diffusion-based generative modeling for ligand-specific complex generation and an extended neural relational inference (NRI) framework for trajectory-level interaction analysis. NeuralPlexer was applied to a library of 3094 FDA-approved drugs to generate BCL-2-ligand complex conformations at scale, yielding 1294 structurally accepta
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study presents a multimodal computational pipeline for drug repurposing targeting the cancer protein BCL-2, combining diffusion-based generative models to predict drug-protein complex structures with neural relational inference to analyze how ligand binding reshapes residue-level communication dynamics. The workflow was applied to 3,094 FDA-approved drugs, yielding 1,294 structurally acceptable BCL-2-ligand complexes, with select candidates validated in vitro.

papers.title: Elucidating the beneficial effects of gut microbiota-derived metabolites in treating hepatocellular carcinoma: an integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and single-cell sequencing analysis.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common type of liver cancer and the third leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While accumulating evidence has highlighted the beneficial effects of gut microbiota (GM)-derived metabolites in HCC treatment, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We retrieved GM-derived metabolites from gutMGene v2.0, acquired their targets using the Similarity Ensemble Approach (SEA) and Swiss Target Prediction (STP), and identified HCC-related targets from public databases. Overlapping targets were then obtained via Venn diagram analysis. We constr
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, molecular docking, and single-cell sequencing to investigate how gut microbiota-derived metabolites may help treat hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The authors identified overlapping targets between microbiota metabolites and HCC-related genes, then used docking and single-cell data to explore potential mechanisms. The work provides a computational framework for understanding microbiota-metabolite-host interactions in liver cancer.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a computational systems-biology method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize promising combinations of targeted therapies. By identifying and mitigating non-response signatures, the approach narrows the vast space of possible drug pairs to those most likely to overcome primary non-response.

papers.title: A‑iMPO: A Design-Time Prediction Toolbox for Blood Brain Barrier Permeation Using an Integrated and Interpretable Multiparameter Optimization Framework.
papers.abstract: Design time prioritization of central nervous system (CNS) drug candidates remains a challenge due to the restrictive nature of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) governing brain exposure. Although various multiparameter optimization (MPO) strategies have guided CNS medicinal chemistry for over a decade, existing frameworks rely heavily on heuristic cutoffs and offer limited interpretability across chemically diverse scaffolds. Here, we introduce a next generation CNS-MPO frameworkAragen-iMPO, (A-iMPO)which was developed using 5,129 curated compounds through an integrated workflow combining expla
papers.summary: The authors present A-iMPO, a design-time prediction toolbox for blood-brain barrier permeation that uses an integrated, interpretable multiparameter optimization framework trained on 5,129 curated compounds. It aims to improve on existing CNS-MPO strategies that rely on heuristic cutoffs and lack interpretability across diverse chemical scaffolds.

papers.title: Leveraging neural network models for drug repurposing: a case study on cardiac hypertrophy.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing has emerged as an attractive strategy in contemporary pharmaceutical research, presenting an opportunity to expedite drug discovery, minimize developmental costs, and mitigate risks associated with developing new pharmaceuticals. In this study, we investigated a novel approach based on deep learning of human transcriptomic mechanisms for systematic identification of additional therapeutic potential in preexisting drugs. We trained a composite feedforward neural network model using gene expression data sourced from the ARCHS4 compilation of the GEO, encompassing extensive human
papers.summary: This study trains a feedforward neural network on human transcriptomic data from ARCHS4 to predict drug repurposing candidates, applying it to cardiac hypertrophy. The model identifies existing drugs with potential new therapeutic effects by learning gene expression signatures associated with the disease.

papers.title: Global Research Trends and Insights on AI Usage in Tuberculosis: Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge despite prevention efforts. AI offers promising approaches to long-standing challenges in TB diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management; however, a systematic mapping of global research priorities and translational gaps in AI applications to TB is currently lacking.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis systematically maps global research trends and priorities in AI applications for tuberculosis, covering areas such as diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management. It identifies translational gaps between AI research output and clinical implementation, providing a landscape view of where the field is heading.

papers.title: From QSAR to deep learning: an interpretable comprehensive pipeline with a read-across approach for mutagenicity prediction via the Enalos Cloud Platform.
papers.abstract: Assessing the mutagenicity of chemical compounds is essential for ensuring their safe handling and use, thereby minimizing potential health risks. New approach methodologies (NAMs), including computational approaches, provide non-animal alternatives for testing novel materials and chemicals. This study highlights the potential of in silico NAMs, which can contribute to the development of novel Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) chemicals and substances by identifying potentially hazardous ones at an early stage. Emphasis is given to the mutagenicity prediction based on data from the Ames (b
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable computational pipeline that combines QSAR modeling, deep learning, and a read-across approach to predict chemical mutagenicity using Ames test data. The workflow is deployed as a user-friendly tool on the Enalos Cloud Platform, supporting non-animal alternatives for chemical safety assessment. It aims to aid early-stage identification of hazardous substances in Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) initiatives.

papers.title: Decision-grade evidence for AI-enabled small-molecule discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now guides choices across small-molecule discovery, yet benchmark gains rarely reveal whether a model changed the next compound, assay or project decision. This Perspective organizes public evidence around Design, Make, Test and Analyze (DMTA) handoffs. It distinguishes reproducible benchmark evidence (C1), use-relevant retrospective robustness (C2), executed Make or Test handoffs (C3), prospective workflow comparisons (C4-W) and traceable downstream trajectories (C4-D), with separate Evaluation, Deliverability and Governance profiles. Two authors independently screened
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This Perspective argues that AI benchmarks for small-molecule discovery often fail to show whether models actually influenced real project decisions. It proposes a tiered evidence framework (C1–C4) organized around Design-Make-Test-Analyze handoffs, distinguishing reproducible benchmarks from executed handoffs and prospective workflow comparisons, along with Evaluation, Deliverability, and Governance profiles.

papers.title: An interpretable framework applying protein words to predict protein-small molecule complementary pairing rules.
papers.abstract: Despite the high accuracy of 'black box' deep learning models, drug discovery still relies on protein-ligand interaction principles and heuristics. To improve interpretability of protein-small molecule binding predictions, we developed the PWRules framework, which applies binding affinity data to identify privileged small molecule fragments and subsequently defines complementary pairing rules between these fragments and protein words (semantic sequence units) through an interpretability module. The resulting word-fragment rules are then used by the PWScore function to prioritize active compoun
papers.summary: The authors present PWRules, an interpretable framework that learns 'protein words' (semantic sequence units) and pairs them with privileged small-molecule fragments using binding affinity data, yielding explicit complementary pairing rules. These rules feed a PWScore function that prioritizes active compounds, offering a transparent alternative to black-box deep learning models for protein-small molecule binding prediction.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Prediction of Dose-Linear Pharmacokinetics: Utilizing Molecular Descriptors to Guide Formulation Strategy.
papers.abstract: Early stage preclinical drug formulation development can be impacted by limited materials and time, especially when making rapid, data-driven decisions is critical. An important parameter to consider is dose linearity, as this can guide the selection between determining if a conventional or enabled formulation strategy is necessary to achieve the expected target exposure as the dose is escalated. This work explores the application of machine learning models to predict dose linearity for compounds administered to the mouse species based on the molecular properties. We utilize a diverse set of m
papers.summary: This study applies machine learning models to predict whether drug compounds will exhibit dose-linear pharmacokinetics in mice, using molecular descriptors as inputs. The goal is to help formulation scientists decide early in preclinical development whether a conventional or enabling formulation strategy is needed, saving time and material.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the two method classes succeed for different reasons, with performance diverging notably under realistic cross-docking scenarios. The work highlights that no single approach dominates and that determinants of success differ between physics-based and AI-driven methods.

papers.title: Integrated Pharmacogenomic and Structure-Guided Analyses Link LCC-10 (NSC765599) to an MMP-Associated Extracellular Matrix Regulatory Network in Leukemia.
papers.abstract: Leukemia progression is increasingly shaped by reciprocal interactions between leukemic cells and the bone marrow microenvironment, yet the extracellular regulatory networks associated with these interactions remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the biological context associated with the antileukemic activity of LCC-10 (NSC765599), a synthetic biphenyl benzamide derivative, using an integrated pharmacogenomic and structure-guided computational framework. Antiproliferative activity was first characterized using the NCI-60 screen and subsequently integrated with pharmacogenomic
papers.summary: This study uses pharmacogenomic profiling and structure-guided computational analysis to link the antileukemic compound LCC-10 (NSC765599) to an extracellular matrix regulatory network involving matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in leukemia. The findings suggest that LCC-10's activity may be tied to disruption of leukemia-microenvironment interactions, highlighting a potential MMP-associated therapeutic axis.

papers.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence with Emerging Pharmaceutical Technologies: Current Progress, Clinical Translation, and Future Challenges.
papers.abstract: Modern scientific and technological developments are driving major advances in drug research and development. This narrative review, based on a structured search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (2018-2026), examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are accelerating a historically prolonged and expensive process, alongside pharmacogenomics, organ-on-a-chip systems, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, and nanotechnology. In benchmark studies, deep learning techniques have achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of over 0.85 for a
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how AI and machine learning are being combined with emerging pharmaceutical technologies—including pharmacogenomics, organ-on-a-chip systems, 3D bioprinting, and nanotechnology—to speed up drug research and development. It highlights benchmark results such as deep learning models achieving AUROC above 0.85, and discusses clinical translation progress alongside remaining challenges.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven identification of PIM2 kinase inhibitors through QSAR modeling and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The proto-oncogene serine/threonine kinase PIM2 is a critical regulator of cell proliferation, survival, and tumor progression and represents an attractive therapeutic target for several cancers. In this study, an integrated machine learning-guided computational pipeline was developed to identify potential PIM2 inhibitors by combining quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and pharmacokinetic prediction. Bioactivity data for PIM2 inhibitors were retrieved from the ChEMBL database, yielding 5953 co
papers.summary: This study developed a computational pipeline combining QSAR modeling, virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and pharmacokinetic prediction to identify potential inhibitors of the PIM2 kinase, a cancer drug target. Using bioactivity data from ChEMBL, the authors built machine learning models to screen compound libraries and prioritize candidate inhibitors. The work demonstrates an integrated in silico workflow for early-stage drug discovery targeting PIM2.

papers.title: HighFold4: extending AlphaFold3 to accurate cyclic peptide conformation prediction via custom chemical connectivity.
papers.abstract: While AlphaFold3 has revolutionized protein structure prediction and supports noncanonical amino acids, its architecture always fails to reliably generate the closed-ring topologies characteristic of cyclic peptides. Existing adaptations, such as imposing distance constraints via an offset matrix, enforce ring geometry but cannot specify the chemical identity of the cyclization bond, leading to a restrictive bias toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles. Here, we present HighFold4, a framework that adapts AlphaFold3 to explicitly incorporate user-defined chemical connectivity between resi
papers.summary: HighFold4 extends AlphaFold3 to accurately predict cyclic peptide structures by explicitly incorporating user-defined chemical connectivity for the cyclization bond, rather than relying on generic distance constraints. This overcomes AlphaFold3's bias toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles and its general failure to reliably generate closed-ring topologies. The framework enables more accurate modeling of diverse cyclic peptide scaffolds.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered High-Content Analysis: Methodologies and Applications in Bioactive Compound Discovery from Natural Sources.
papers.abstract: High-content screening (HCS) is a useful phenotypic drug discovery technology that combines automated microscopy, image analysis, and high-throughput experimentation to comprehensively characterize biological responses to diverse perturbations. This review summarizes the methodological fundamentals of high-content analysis, including image preprocessing, cell segmentation, feature processing, and downstream analysis, as well as the diverse phenotypic datasets generated from different biological models, perturbation strategies, and staining approaches. Recent advances in artificial intelligence
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being integrated into high-content screening (HCS) pipelines, covering image preprocessing, cell segmentation, feature extraction, and downstream phenotypic analysis. It also catalogs the phenotypic datasets generated from different biological models, perturbation strategies, and staining approaches, with a focus on discovering bioactive compounds from natural sources.

papers.title: Heat Shock Proteins in Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Targeting.
papers.abstract: Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are molecular chaperones that couple proteostasis to cancer metabolic reprogramming under oncogenic and microenvironmental stress. This Review integrates structural, biochemical, preclinical, and clinical evidence on HSP90, HSP70, HSP60, HSP40, HSP110, and small HSPs. We explain how ATPase cycles, chaperonin cages, co-chaperone networks, and organelle-specific localization stabilize metabolic enzymes, glucose transporters, hypoxia-responsive factors, and electron-transport-chain components, thereby coordinating glycolysis, mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox homeostas
papers.summary: This review synthesizes structural, biochemical, preclinical, and clinical evidence on how heat shock proteins (HSP90, HSP70, HSP60, HSP40, HSP110, and small HSPs) act as molecular chaperones that link protein homeostasis to cancer metabolic reprogramming. It details how ATPase cycles, chaperonin cages, co-chaperone networks, and organelle-specific localization stabilize metabolic enzymes, glucose transporters, hypoxia-responsive factors, and electron transport chain components, thereby coordinating glycolysis, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and redox homeostasis. The review also discusses therapeutic strategies for targeting HSPs in cancer.

papers.title: PMPIHGLL: predicting metabolite-protein interactions using dual hypergraph convolutional networks and large language models.
papers.abstract: Metabolite-protein interactions (MPIs) play pivotal roles in regulating cellular processes and metabolic pathways and have important implications for systems biology and drug discovery. Although several computational models have been proposed, alternative approaches are needed to broaden the methodological toolkit for MPI prediction. In this study, we developed a new deep-learning model for predicting MPIs. Chemical and protein large language models were used to generate informative representations of metabolites and proteins. For each entity type, we constructed two K-nearest-neighbor hypergr
papers.summary: This paper introduces PMPIHGLL, a deep-learning model that predicts interactions between metabolites and proteins by combining chemical and protein large language models with dual hypergraph convolutional networks. The approach generates informative representations of metabolites and proteins and models higher-order relationships via K-nearest-neighbor hypergraphs, aiming to broaden the computational toolkit for metabolite-protein interaction prediction. The work is relevant to systems biology and drug discovery applications.

papers.title: MSF-HierGNN: a multi-source substructure-fusion hierarchical GNN method and web server to predict molecular property for drug design.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the biological and physicochemical properties of molecules is of great significance in shortening the process and decreasing the failure rate of drug design. Thus, previous studies have established several benchmark datasets and developed several Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) based artificial intelligence (AI) predictive methods. However, since these methods encounter challenges such as incomplete representation of molecular hierarchical structures, insufficient exploration of local topological features, and under-extraction of correlations among atomic features, our stud
papers.summary: The authors present MSF-HierGNN, a hierarchical graph neural network that fuses multi-source substructure information to better capture molecular hierarchical structure, local topology, and atomic feature correlations for predicting molecular properties. They also provide a web server for drug design applications. The method aims to improve accuracy over existing GNN-based property predictors.

papers.title: DFRL-Mol: a dual-stage framework of reinforcement learning for multi-scenario molecule optimization.
papers.abstract: As a critical step in drug discovery, molecule optimization aims to improve specific properties of lead compounds. Inspired by isosteres (i.e. molecular substructures with similar reactive electron shells), existing AI-based methods have been proposed for molecule optimization. However, they often rely on available matched molecular pairs (MMPs), thus facing two essential challenges. First, the limited diversity of available MMPs leads to biased training and a lack of novelty in the optimized molecules, in both single-objective (SO) and multi-objective (MO) optimization. Second, the low number
papers.summary: DFRL-Mol introduces a dual-stage reinforcement learning framework for molecule optimization that addresses two key limitations of existing AI methods: reliance on limited matched molecular pairs (MMPs) that causes biased training and low novelty, and poor performance in multi-objective optimization. The approach aims to improve both single-objective and multi-objective molecule optimization for drug discovery by overcoming the diversity constraints of MMP-based training data.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, Antimycobacterial Evaluation, and In Silico Investigation of Benzisothiazole-Based Hydrazide Derivatives as Potential Anti-Tuberculosis Agents.
papers.abstract: A series of novel benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives was rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated for their antitubercular activity. Among the synthesized compounds, derivative 8k emerged as the most potent candidate, exhibiting a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.25 μg/mL, along with a high selectivity index (SI) of 42 and confirmed bactericidal activity. To gain preliminary insights into its possible mechanism of action, compound 8k was subjected to molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, using enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (InhA) as the
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives and tested them against tuberculosis bacteria. The most potent compound, 8k, showed strong activity (MIC 0.25 μg/mL) with good selectivity and bactericidal effects, and docking simulations suggest it may work by inhibiting the InhA enzyme. These findings highlight a promising new scaffold for anti-TB drug development.

papers.title: Repurposing antifungal drugs for Oral squamous cell carcinoma using network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics approaches.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains an important cause of cancer morbidity and mortality, and new multi-target approaches are required to increase therapeutic options. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to identify new anticancer applications for clinically approved drugs with established safety profiles. An integrative in silico workflow was designed to identify overlapping targets between selected antifungal drugs and OSCC-associated genes based on network pharmacology and protein-protein interaction analysis. Network pharmacology identified 144 common targets for antifunga
papers.summary: This study uses an in silico drug repurposing pipeline combining network pharmacology, protein-protein interaction analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics to identify antifungal drugs that could be repurposed for oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The authors found 144 shared targets between antifungal drugs and OSCC-associated genes, suggesting multi-target therapeutic potential. The work is computational only and would require experimental validation.

papers.title: Cannabis as a source of novel therapeutics: A computational study combining LBDD and structure-based docking/dynamics to identify novel drug-like compounds for colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Cannabis represents a valuable source of bioactive compounds with significant therapeutic potential, thanks to its rich phytochemical profile, making it a prime candidate for cancer research. Our study investigates the potential of cannabis-derived compounds to inhibit cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2), a crucial regulator of cell-cycle progression and colorectal cancer cell proliferation. A comprehensive computational workflow integrating 3D-QSAR modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, drug-likeness assessment, and ADMET prediction was employed to investigate a dataset of
papers.summary: This computational study screens cannabis-derived phytochemicals for their ability to inhibit CDK2, a key cell-cycle regulator implicated in colorectal cancer proliferation. Using an integrated workflow of 3D-QSAR modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET/drug-likeness prediction, the authors identify candidate compounds with favorable binding and pharmacokinetic profiles. The findings suggest cannabis metabolites warrant further experimental validation as potential CDK2-targeted anticancer leads.

papers.title: Integrative multi-transcriptomics and network pharmacology reveal natural therapeutics as anti-cancer agents targeting AURKA for ovarian cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains one of the most lethal gynecologic malignancies, largely because it is often diagnosed late, recurs frequently, and develops resistance to conventional chemotherapy. These challenges emphasize the urgent need for novel and less toxic therapeutic strategies. In this study, we applied an integrative in silico workflow combining transcriptomic analysis, network biology, pan-cancer exploration, and computational drug discovery to identify potential phytochemical inhibitors targeting Aurora kinase A (AURKA) in OC. Differential gene expression analysis of three GEO datase
papers.summary: This study used an integrative in silico pipeline combining transcriptomic analysis, network biology, and computational drug discovery to identify phytochemical inhibitors targeting AURKA in ovarian cancer. The authors analyzed GEO datasets to find differentially expressed genes, then used network pharmacology to prioritize natural compounds as potential anti-cancer agents. The work nominates AURKA as a therapeutic target and proposes plant-derived compounds for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative In Silico Profiling of Major Phytochemicals From a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum Mixture: Docking, Molecular Dynamics, ADMET, and Ligand-Based Target Prediction on Shared Pathways in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) converge through metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and impaired neuronal signaling, providing a rationale for multi-target intervention. This study aimed to identify phytochemicals from a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum mixture that may modulate this disease axis. Seven constituents were screened against AChE, BACE1, DPP4, glucokinase, GSK3β, and TACE using molecular docking and MM-GBSA rescoring. Prioritized complexes underwent triplicate 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, post-MD MM-GBSA analysis, physicoch
papers.summary: This study used computational docking, molecular dynamics, ADMET, and ligand-based target prediction to screen seven phytochemicals from a Sclerocarya birrea-Nauclea latifolia-Piper longum mixture against six protein targets shared between type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease. The work identifies candidate natural compounds that may modulate the convergent metabolic-inflammatory axis of both diseases, though findings remain purely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: KGTC-DDA:Drug-disease association prediction based on parallel graph isomorphism and transformer networks with cross-attention.
papers.abstract: Drug development is a complex, time-consuming, and costly process, making drug repurposing an important strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Computational drug-disease association (DDA) prediction has therefore attracted increasing attention in recent years. Although many existing methods incorporate similarity information and graph neural networks for DDA prediction, effectively capturing both local structural patterns and global dependencies, as well as modeling complex interactions between drugs and diseases, remains challenging. To address these limitat
papers.summary: This paper introduces KGTC-DDA, a computational framework for predicting drug-disease associations to support drug repurposing. The method combines parallel graph isomorphism networks with transformer networks and cross-attention to capture both local structural patterns and global dependencies in drug-disease interaction graphs. The approach aims to improve prediction accuracy over existing similarity- and GNN-based methods.

papers.title: DLRNA-BERTa: a transformer approach for predicting molecule-RNA binding affinities.
papers.abstract: Therapies targeting RNA are rapidly expanding, with 24 FDA-approved RNA therapeutics and over 130 currently in clinical trials, highlighting RNA's growing role in drug discovery. In this context, transformer-based language models provide a scalable and cost-effective approach to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by enabling the prediction of molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This study introduces DLRNA-BERTa, a RoBERTa-based framework that integrates RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to model molecule-RNA binding affinities. The framework includes six RNA class-
papers.summary: DLRNA-BERTa is a RoBERTa-based deep learning framework that combines RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to predict binding affinities between small molecules and RNA directly from sequence information. This addresses a growing need in RNA-targeted drug discovery, where 24 FDA-approved RNA therapeutics and over 130 clinical trials highlight RNA as an emerging drug target class.

papers.title: Combining Phytochemical and Computational Approach on Citrus hystrix DC. (Kaffir Lime) Peel Extract: Anti-Diabetic and Anti-Inflammatory Activities.
papers.abstract: The peel of Citrus hystrix DC. (kaffir lime), an underexploited agro-industrial by-product, may have bioactives. This work tested the ethanolic extract of C. hystrix peel's (EeChP) phytochemicals by GC-MS profiling, and the antidiabetic effect was evaluated using the alpha-amylase inhibitory test, and the anti-inflammatory activity was done using the human red blood cell (HRBC) membrane model. The antibacterial effect was determined using the agar well diffusion method against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. Major constituents subjected to pharmacokinetic and ADMET filtering, molec
papers.summary: This study profiled the phytochemicals in kaffir lime peel extract using GC-MS and tested its antidiabetic, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial activities in vitro. Major compounds were then subjected to pharmacokinetic and ADMET filtering and molecular docking to identify potential bioactive candidates. The work highlights an underused agro-industrial by-product as a source of compounds with possible therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus: Distribution in reproductive organs and integrated biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: While the chemical constituents of flower buds from several Panax species have been reported, the phytochemical profile of the flower buds of Vietnamese ginseng remains understudied, particularly alkaloids. This study aimed to characterize alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus (PVF), investigate their distribution across reproductive plant parts, and their biological relevance.
papers.summary: This study characterizes novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus, a previously understudied Vietnamese ginseng variety. The authors examine how these alkaloids are distributed across different reproductive organs and evaluate their biological activities. The work expands the known phytochemical profile of Panax species and highlights the potential medicinal relevance of alkaloids in ginseng flower buds.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors: Molecular docking, ADMET, Network pharmacology, Molecular dynamics simulation, and DFT studies" [Pharmaceutic. Sci. Adv. 4 (2026) 100108].
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.pscia.2026.100108.].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum notice correcting an earlier article that computationally screened Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors using molecular docking, ADMET, network pharmacology, molecular dynamics, and DFT studies. It contains no new scientific findings, only corrections to the original publication.

papers.title: Computational evaluation of EPA-PC binding to GCase in neuronopathic Gaucher disease.
papers.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient acid β-glucosidase (GCase) activity and consequent accumulation of glucosylceramide. Current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies improve several systemic manifestations but have limited impact on neuronopathic disease, motivating evaluation of alternative molecular strategies. This study computationally assessed the interaction of EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, with human GCase (PDB ID: 2NSX). The protein structure was examined by Ramachandran analysis and hydroph
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics to assess how EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, binds to the lysosomal enzyme GCase, which is deficient in Gaucher disease. The work explores whether this interaction could offer an alternative molecular strategy for neuronopathic forms of the disease, where current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies are largely ineffective.

papers.title: GDA-Pred: Generative AI-Driven Data Augmentation for Improved Prediction of IL-6 and IL-13-Inducing Peptides.
papers.abstract: Identifying interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-13 (IL-13)-inducing peptides is important for drug discovery targeting cancer, immune disorders, and infectious diseases. However, experimental screening is costly and time-consuming. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed that distinguish functional peptides from no-function ones, but their performance is limited by the small number of experimentally validated peptides. In this study, we propose a generative AI-driven data augmentation framework, GDA, and its prediction system, GDA-Pred, to improve the performance of stat
papers.summary: GDA-Pred uses generative AI to create synthetic peptide sequences that augment the small set of experimentally validated IL-6- and IL-13-inducing peptides, then trains a predictor on the enlarged dataset. This data augmentation approach improves prediction accuracy for identifying immunomodulatory peptides relevant to cancer, immune disorders, and infectious disease drug discovery.

papers.title: The Dual Face of Gingival Mesenchymal Stem Cell Paracrine Signalling in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Pro-Tumour Transcriptional Programme and a Hypothesis-Generating Drug-Repurposing Screen.
papers.abstract: Background: In our companion study, the gingival mesenchymal stem cell (GMSC) secretome suppresses oxidative stress and induces apoptosis in primary oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, where those wet-lab results are themselves reported as preliminary; here we ask whether it also engages a proliferation × migration programme in patient tissue. The two arms differ in read-out type (apoptosis and redox there, transcript abundance here), not in opposed function. Methods: Primary OSCC cells received GMSC-conditioned medium (GMSC-CM) or indirect Transwell co-culture, assayed by RT-qPCR (VEGF
papers.summary: This study examines how paracrine signals from gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) affect oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, finding that GMSC-conditioned medium induces a pro-tumour transcriptional programme related to proliferation and migration. The authors also perform a hypothesis-generating drug-repurposing screen, highlighting the dual, context-dependent nature of GMSC paracrine signalling in OSCC.

papers.title: Polyphenol-Rich Opuntia ficus-indica Cladodes: An Integrated Metabolomic, In Vivo and In Silico Study Supporting Their Hypolipidemic and Hepatoprotective Effects.
papers.abstract: Background: Hyperlipidemia is a major risk factor for cardiometabolic disorders, including non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and is closely associated with oxidative stress. Opuntia ficus-indica (OFI) cladodes are recognized as a rich source of bioactive phytochemicals; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying their metabolic benefits remain incompletely understood. Objectives: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the hypolipidemic and hepatoprotective potential of a polyphenol-rich O. ficus-indica cladode extract (OCE) using an integrated approach combining in vivo evalua
papers.summary: This study combined metabolomic profiling, in vivo animal experiments, and in silico modeling to investigate how a polyphenol-rich extract from Opuntia ficus-indica cladodes (cactus pads) reduces blood lipids and protects the liver. The extract showed hypolipidemic and hepatoprotective effects in hyperlipidemic animals, with computational analyses suggesting molecular mechanisms involving oxidative stress pathways. The work supports the traditional use of cactus cladodes as a functional food against cardiometabolic disorders like NAFLD.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in experimental and clinical in vitro analysis: applications, limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into in vitro analyses represents a transformative shift in laboratory medicine, diagnostics, and pharmaceutical research. Traditional in vitro methods, from cell culture assays to high-throughput screening, rely on manual interpretation and conventional statistics. Machine and deep learning now automate image analysis, improve diagnostic accuracy, accelerate drug discovery, and enhance quality control. Convolutional neural networks and predictive models have reported specialist-level performance in cell segmentation, biomarker detection, and patholog
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning and deep learning are being integrated into in vitro laboratory workflows, including cell culture assays, high-throughput screening, and pathology. It highlights applications such as automated image analysis, cell segmentation, biomarker detection, and quality control, while discussing current limitations and future directions for AI in experimental and clinical in vitro analysis.

papers.title: Integrating artificial intelligence across the cancer drug discovery pipeline using a design-test-refine workflow.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence-driven drug design (AIDD) is increasingly transforming cancer drug discovery, but its applications are often considered as individual computational tasks rather than interconnected stages of the drug discovery pipeline. This mini-review addresses this gap by firstly identifying the following four interconnected stages of anticancer drug development (1) target identification and biomarker-guided prioritization (2), structure-based and generative molecular design (3), perturbational mechanism-of-action assessment, and (4) drug response, resistance, and combination priorit
papers.summary: This mini-review argues that AI applications in cancer drug discovery should be viewed as interconnected stages of a single design-test-refine pipeline rather than isolated computational tasks. It organizes the field into four linked stages: target identification and biomarker prioritization, structure-based and generative molecular design, perturbational mechanism-of-action assessment, and drug response/resistance/combination prediction.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in obesity management: clinical evidence, translational gaps, and implementation priorities-a structured narrative review.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a chronic, relapsing disease that requires long-term lifestyle treatment, pharmacotherapy, and metabolic and bariatric surgery. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being studied across these pathways, but its clinical readiness varies substantially. This Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA)-informed structured narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar through 1 June 2026, primarily for literature published since 2015, with citation chaining used to identify earlier landmark studies. Evidence was appr
papers.summary: This structured narrative review examines how artificial intelligence is being applied across obesity management pathways, including lifestyle interventions, pharmacotherapy, and metabolic/bariatric surgery. The authors find that clinical readiness of AI tools varies widely across these domains and identify translational gaps and implementation priorities for moving AI into routine obesity care.

papers.title: Uncharted phytochemical frontiers: a systematic review of novel bioactive compounds from underexplored aromatic plants for cancer therapy.
papers.abstract: Cancer continues to cause a high degree of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making it essential for new, safer, and more effective therapies to be developed. Aromatic plants provide researchers with diverse secondary metabolites that may have useful pharmacological effects. This systematic review examines several aromatic plants that were used medicinally in the past but have not been examined recently for their potential to produce new bioactive molecules with anticancer activity.
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys underexplored aromatic plants for novel bioactive secondary metabolites with potential anticancer activity. It highlights plants historically used medicinally but neglected in modern drug discovery, cataloging candidate compounds and their reported mechanisms. The work aims to direct future research toward these phytochemical frontiers for cancer therapy development.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in rheumatoid arthritis: current applications and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a highly prevalent systemic autoimmune disease characterized by a complex and partially understood pathogenesis. The substantial challenges in early identification and marked therapeutic heterogeneity pose a significant burden on affected patients. Despite notable advancements in diagnostic techniques and therapeutic interventions in recent years, optimal patient care remains hindered by several ongoing clinical challenges. To address these limitations, artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into the field of rheumatology. By leveraging its p
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being applied to rheumatoid arthritis, covering current uses and future directions. It highlights AI's potential to improve early diagnosis and address treatment heterogeneity in RA patients. The paper surveys the field rather than presenting new experimental data.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of AI innovations for tackling antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global public health concern, rendering available antimicrobials ineffective and leading to infections that are difficult to treat. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly applied across the AMR continuum, including resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, new antimicrobial discovery, drug repurposing, antimicrobial surveillance, and clinical decision support. In this review, we aim to highlight recent developments in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR). In addition, we review computatio
papers.summary: This review surveys recent applications of artificial intelligence across the antimicrobial resistance landscape, covering resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, novel antimicrobial discovery, drug repurposing, surveillance, and clinical decision support. It synthesizes how computational and machine learning approaches are being deployed to address the growing global challenge of drug-resistant infections.

papers.title: Drug Repurposing for Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease: Current Evidence, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a prevalent chronic liver condition with limited approved pharmacotherapies. Drug repurposing offers a time-efficient alternative to de novo development, yet existing reviews often compile candidate compounds without critically appraising the methodological robustness, evidence quality, or translational barriers. In this review, we evaluated current repurposing strategies, including real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validations. As a preliminary search for this review, we searched PubMed and clini
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates drug repurposing strategies for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), covering real-world data analyses, computational screening, and experimental validation approaches. Unlike prior reviews that simply list candidate compounds, it appraises the methodological rigor, evidence quality, and translational barriers facing repurposing efforts for this common liver condition with few approved therapies.

papers.title: Cross-fusion of digital twins and artificial intelligence in diabetes: from mechanistic elucidation to full-cycle precision management.
papers.abstract: The integration of digital twins (DT) and artificial intelligence (AI) is driving a paradigm shift in diabetes mellitus (DM) care from traditional population-based, symptomatic intervention to a lifecycle-oriented precision management approach. This review systematically elaborates on the cross-disciplinary integration mechanisms of the two technologies. By integrating multimodal data and constructing physiologically constrained hybrid models, it achieves multi-scale mechanistic analyses ranging from single-cell β-cell protection to multi-organ complications at the basic research level. On the
papers.summary: This review describes how combining digital twins with artificial intelligence could transform diabetes care from population-level symptom treatment to personalized, lifecycle-oriented precision management. It highlights the use of multimodal data and physiologically constrained hybrid models to analyze mechanisms ranging from single-cell β-cell protection to multi-organ complications.

papers.title: Structure-based molecular modeling of a novel S-Remiketamine scaffold and derived arylcyclohexanone analogues: NMDA receptor dynamics, MM-GBSA ranking, and CES1-Oriented structural compatibility.
papers.abstract: Short-acting ketamine-related scaffold design remains an important medicinal-chemistry problem, but computational studies require conservative interpretation until receptor, enzymatic, and pharmacokinetic validation is available.
papers.summary: This computational study models a novel S-Remiketamine scaffold and related arylcyclohexanone analogues, examining their interactions with the NMDA receptor through molecular dynamics and MM-GBSA binding free energy ranking, plus structural compatibility with the metabolic enzyme CES1. The work is exploratory and the authors caution that findings require experimental validation of receptor binding, enzymatic processing, and pharmacokinetics before any conclusions can be drawn.

papers.title: From in silico prediction to experimental validation: Identification of drugs and novel synergistic combinations that inhibit growth of inflammatory breast cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing can accelerate the identification of novel therapeutic candidates for rare cancers such as inflammatory breast cancer (IBC), an aggressive type with limited therapeutic options. Here, we report an experimental validation study of compounds previously identified through two computational approaches: Literature Wide Association Studies (LWAS) and Gene Reversal Rate (GRR). Candidate compounds were tested using orthogonal cell viability assays in 2D models across IBC and non-IBC cell lines. In the SUM149 IBC cell line, repurposed compounds predicted from LWAS achieved a 70% succes
papers.summary: This study experimentally validated drug repurposing candidates for inflammatory breast cancer that were previously identified through two computational approaches (Literature Wide Association Studies and Gene Reversal Rate). Compounds were tested using cell viability assays across IBC and non-IBC cell lines, with LWAS-predicted compounds achieving a 70% success rate in the SUM149 IBC cell line. The work demonstrates that computational predictions can yield experimentally confirmed drugs and novel synergistic combinations for this aggressive cancer type.

papers.title: Human organoids and organ-on-chip systems for AI-guided therapeutic discovery against emerging and re-emerging infections.
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging infections expose a persistent mismatch between the speed of pathogen evolution and the pace of therapeutic development. Conventional two-dimensional cultures are scalable but poorly reproduce tissue architecture, whereas animal models may not capture human-specific tropism, immunity, pharmacokinetics, or toxicity. Human organoids and organ-on-chip systems offer complementary solutions by combining organ-specific human cells with three-dimensional architecture, barrier function, perfusion, mechanical forces, and, increasingly, immune and microbial components. This revi
papers.summary: This review discusses how human organoids and organ-on-chip systems can bridge the gap between simple 2D cultures and animal models for studying emerging and re-emerging infections. It highlights how these platforms reproduce human-specific tissue architecture, immunity, and drug responses, and how they can be paired with AI to accelerate therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis indicates MARCO and ZBTB20 as candidate biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients have a clearly increased possibility to develop tuberculosis (TB). However, the common molecular background, useful diagnostic molecules, and treatment-related targets of this comorbidity are still not sufficiently explained. We attempted to search the shared genetic factors and candidate drug targets for RA and TB by an integrated multi-omics way.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify shared molecular features between rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis, two conditions that frequently co-occur. The authors pinpoint MARCO and ZBTB20 as candidate biomarkers and potential drug targets linking the two diseases.

papers.title: Thymol and Limonene as Potent Antimicrobials: Bridging In Vitro Efficacy and Molecular Docking Insights.
papers.abstract: Nowadays, antimicrobial resistance has created an urgent need for elaborating effective and novel antibiotic agents. In effect, bioactive compounds derived from plants have attracted great interest due to their biological activities. This work intended to study and compare the antimicrobial effect of thymol and limonene against multiple clinical microorganisms including gram-positive bacteria, gram-negative bacteria, yeasts, and mycobacteria. Molecular docking and bioavailability prediction of thymol and limonene were also performed. The in vitro study was realized via disk diffusion technique
papers.summary: This study compares the antimicrobial activity of two plant-derived compounds, thymol and limonene, against a range of clinical pathogens including gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, yeasts, and mycobacteria. The authors also used molecular docking and bioavailability predictions to explore how these compounds might interact with microbial targets, linking in vitro efficacy with computational insights.

papers.title: Catechins as antibiofilm agents: molecular insights for virtual screening and in vitro biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Bacterial Biofilms are of great concern because they are the main drivers of antimicrobial resistance. We investigated the potential of catechins against bacterial biofilms using advanced computational and in vitro models.
papers.summary: This study investigates catechins, a class of natural polyphenols, as potential agents against bacterial biofilms, which are major contributors to antimicrobial resistance. Using computational virtual screening and in vitro biological assays, the authors identify and evaluate catechin compounds for their antibiofilm activity, providing molecular insights that could guide the development of new antibiofilm therapies.

papers.title: Repurposing MK0873 as a non-covalent hTERT-Targeting compound: a proof of concept study.
papers.abstract: Telomerase is a key regulator of both cellular immortality and aging, making it an attractive target for cancer therapy and age associated pathologies. Its clinical exploitation has been limited by structural complexity and challenges in achieving specificity. Recent structural insights into human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) have enabled the identification of selective inhibitors. Here, we repurposed MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously evaluated in Phase II clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis and COPD, as a non covalent telomerase targeting agent. In silico docking and molecu
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study repurposes MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously tested in Phase II trials for inflammatory diseases, as a non-covalent inhibitor of human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT). Using in silico docking and molecular dynamics, the authors identify MK0873 as a potential telomerase-targeting compound, suggesting a new route to telomerase inhibition for cancer and aging-related pathologies.
